hero.headline: One agent, every account you own
hero.sub: Your agent stops being one Claude account. Sign in to all of them, watch both limits on each, and let a turn move to a freer account before a limit stops it.

shot.alt: Settings, Agents: three Claude accounts in priority order, each with a 5-hour session bar and a weekly bar, and an auto-switch toggle below.
shot.caption: Settings → Agents. The order you drag them into IS the priority.

blocks.title: Every account, signed in at once
blocks.body: Each account gets its own sandbox, so signing into a second one no longer signs you out of the first. A session picks the account it runs on, and you can read any account's limits without switching to it.

shot.alt: Three account rows in priority order: the first at 34% of its 5-hour window and 61% of its weekly one, the second at 7% and 22%, the third at 88% and 73% drawn in amber.
shot.caption: Two bars per account — the 5-hour window and the 7-day one.

blocks.title: And when a limit does land

items.title: It moves before you notice
items.text: The turn switches to a freer account rather than stopping. Auto-switch is a toggle; off, it reports the limit and changes nothing.

items.title: It steers on refusals, not forecasts
items.text: The switch follows the limit the API actually refused, instead of the percentage it predicted you would hit.

items.title: Your order is the tie-break
items.text: Between two equally free accounts, the one higher in your list wins — not the one earlier in the alphabet.

items.title: Every number says how old it is
items.text: A usage reading carries its age, and tells you when a refresh could not move it. No silently stale percentage.

blocks.title: Statuses are yours to declare
blocks.body: Four statuses were hardcoded. Now a project declares its own in one file and they appear on the board. Nothing has to be created in GitHub or ClickUp first: each declared status rides under one of the four shipped ones, so the backend only ever sees the parent and carries your name as a label.

shot.alt: A kanban board with five columns: To Do, In Progress, Blocked, In Review and Needs QA. Blocked and Needs QA were declared by this project.
shot.caption: Blocked and Needs QA exist because this project asked for them.

blocks.title: The brain consolidates itself
blocks.body: Sleep used to wait to be asked. Set the debt levels at which it offers, recommends, then requires a consolidation — and let this machine run the whole flow in the background when the debt gets high, so you stop being asked at all.

shot.alt: Settings → Sleep, showing the Drowsy, Sleepy and Must Sleep debt thresholds, a per-specialist model table, and a background-consolidation toggle.
shot.caption: Thresholds are shared with your team; background sleep stays on this machine.

blocks.title: Settings stopped repeating itself
blocks.body: Four groups, one description each, and no Save button — a change applies when you make it. Two experiments also left the page this version: the OpenUI render mode, and Sleepy's notch capture bar.

shot.alt: The Settings sidebar: Project, Memory, Integrations and This machine, with no Sleepy row.
shot.caption: One grammar for the whole page.

blocks.text: Sleepy the mascot is not going anywhere — it is the notch CAPTURE BAR that was removed, after an experiment that answered no. The mascot still keeps the Sleep page, and "Sleepy" is still the middle rung of the sleep-debt ladder.

items.label: of frozen requests, gone
items.note: the cross-vault team fetch ran on the server's event loop

items.label: network round-trips before first paint
items.note: fonts ship in the bundle instead of loading from Google

items.label: of cold login shell, skipped
items.note: the desktop app now caches where it found the CLI

blocks.title: The app opens faster, for four separate reasons
blocks.body: Nothing here is visible in a screenshot — it is four waits that no longer happen before the launcher is usable. Fonts were blocking first paint on a network request. The team fetch blocked every other request while it ran. Its first fire raced first paint. And the desktop shell paid a full cold shell to find the CLI, on every single launch.

shot.alt: The dreamcontext launcher listing projects, each with its status dot.
shot.caption: The surface all four of those waits used to sit in front of.

items.title: A sub-agent's report is a card
items.text: A finished sub-agent lands as its own named card in the transcript, instead of a wall the main agent re-types at you.

items.title: Plan and Develop end in a clean judge
items.text: Both modes finish with a reviewer that has not read the conversation, rather than the agent marking its own work.

items.title: Lab reports pick one window
items.text: A report declares a measurement window and every item inherits it, so 7-day and 30-day tiles stop sitting side by side. Opening one no longer re-queries everything it references.

items.title: The meeting room got four verbs
items.text: Addressing an agent is free, ASK summons it, WAIT holds it, and a reply lands in the thread you are reading.

closer.title: Add your second account
closer.body: Settings → Agents → Add an account. Drag the list into the order you want sessions to start in.
